title: Living room looking out through the glazed slider to the dining terrace and crape
view_notes: Garden view in the PRODUCTION scene (lane GI): the decided layout LDG-final-B with the real house facade, production exposure group and 24 mm camera. Labelled stand-ins stand for plants with no graded asset; boundary walls, coping, edging, mulch and furniture details are ASSUMED. Not a procurement or planting specification.
assumed: ASSUMED exterior finish: our walls, ground-floor perimeter beams, exposed slab/ramp edges and boundary/fence walls use smooth very light grey-green mineral paint, reflectance 0.65. Entrance steps are paved; soffits are painted white. Neighbour and apartment context remains neutral mineral render; all exposed construction faces receive a stated finish.
False ceilings at 2.70 m (plenum for the flush fittings; the daylight study assumed 2.80 m).
Details added for the render: fluted walnut TV wall, oak headboard slats, glass guard at the stair opening, cove ceilings.

ASSUMED stair fixings: steel base shoe on the stringer holds three-tread frameless laminated glass panels with visible polished edges; glass thickness 12 mm awaits structural design. The wall-side wood handrail uses steel brackets. Risers remain open; coordinate fixings in Revit.

WP4b product fit report (piece -> asset, fits all furnishing checks or keeps the procedural stand-in and why): living-sofa -> sf_minotti_sofa: fits; living-chair-1 -> sf_probber_cane_armchair: fits; living-chair-2 -> sf_probber_cane_armchair: fits; lounge-sofa -> sf_modern_low_sofa: real 3.29 x 1.62 m sofa closes the 914 mm pantry and yard routes with the coffee table beyond its 457 mm front clearance; lounge-armchair -> sf_probber_cane_armchair: fits; cinema-sofa -> sf_cinema_sofa_velvet: product too long for the cinema width; pb-bed -> sf_chelsea_bed: actual mattress geometry required for every berth; dining-table#chair-1 -> sf_dining_chair_boucle: overlap: dining-table / dining-table#chair-1; dining-table#chair-2 -> sf_dining_chair_boucle: overlap: dining-table / dining-table#chair-2; dining-table#chair-3 -> sf_dining_chair_boucle: overlap: dining-table / dining-table#chair-3; dining-table#chair-4 -> sf_dining_chair_boucle: overlap: dining-table / dining-table#chair-4; dining-table#chair-5 -> sf_dining_chair_boucle: overlap: dining-table / dining-table#chair-5; dining-table#chair-6 -> sf_dining_chair_boucle: overlap: dining-table / dining-table#chair-6; study-desk#chair-1 -> modern_arm_chair_01: overlap: study-desk / study-desk#chair-1; study-desk#chair-2 -> modern_arm_chair_01: overlap: study-desk / study-desk#chair-2; study-adult-desk#chair-1 -> modern_arm_chair_01: overlap: study-adult-desk / study-adult-desk#chair-1; ka-desk-1#chair-1 -> sf_kidschair_oak: overlap: ka-desk-1 / ka-desk-1#chair-1; ka-desk-2#chair-1 -> sf_kidschair_oak: overlap: ka-desk-2 / ka-desk-2#chair-1; kb-desk#chair-1 -> sf_kidschair_oak: overlap: kb-desk / kb-desk#chair-1

BEDS: PROCEDURAL BED FALLBACK (stand-in) retained for parents, both kids' rooms and library daybed until a measured, uniformly fitting, neutral-preview-reviewed model is available. Per-part fallback_label records the disclosure without changing view subject identity.
Dressing contents: owned procedural appearances; colours, spacing, forms and unsourced drops ASSUMED. Neufert 1980 p.74 Fig.6 dress/jacket drops. Closed drawers retain hidden contents.
Dressing: clothes on the dressing rails, duvets and pillows on the beds (not design).

ASSUMED furniture detailing: crowned sofa and chair cushions, rounded arms, exposed plinth and legs, and the bunk ladder on its open side; product and fixing details require Revit coordination. Rectangular lofted bed pillows are dressing, not specified products.

ASSUMED joinery details: slim walnut frames and clear architectural glass on the library cabinets, open timber shelves, upholstered daybed mattress and loose cushions, two ergonomic cinema task chairs, microwave drawer in the island, and cleaning-storage doors below the folding counter. Book props are labelled dressing; all builder vertices are checked against their authored envelopes.

By day the basement rooms are shown with their ambient and accent lights at 50 % (a basement is used with lights on by day); bathrooms by day have their lights on; other ground-floor day views are daylight only.
ASSUMED deck-mounted brass bath mixer and spout, three silvered vanity mirrors, coffee machine bodies with trays, spouts and water tanks, and dirty-kitchen canopy and duct; coordinate with Revit.

ASSUMED kitchen products: two worktop coffee machines, island microwave drawer and dirty-kitchen integrated fridge and oven (cleaning storage moves below the folding counter), island downdraft extractor and dirty-kitchen wall hood. Both run sinks and taps are procedural geometry. Product choices and services go into Revit.
ASSUMED hatch reveals and roll-up shutter housing: shutter raised for all current day views; three 0.4 m sliding panels are stowed inside the 0.4 m west pocket, with an overhead track.

ASSUMED bath-fitting bodies and fixing details follow the specified rain heads, hand shower rails, guest bathroom 70 mm flush linear drain and ensuite fixed frameless screen. Guest bathroom and dirty-kitchen ducts remain in the Revit services specification but are omitted from the visible render pending ceiling-void coordination; round ceiling valves and external grilles are shown. the dirty-kitchen cooker hood is the specified extract source. Drip, flow and products remain service selections, not render claims.
Construction details added for the render: 80 mm skirting, 50 mm aluminium window frames and mullions, 70 mm architraves and lever handles (not yet in the Revit model).

Curtains (client 2026-09-28): sheer linen (rough_linen, transmittance 0.55) + a heavy layer on a ceiling track, every bedroom and living-space window and glazed garden door -- blackout (transmittance 0.02) in bedrooms, dim-out (0.10) in living/dining/study. Kitchens, the dirty kitchen, bathrooms/WC and the stair void have none. By day each side stacks to 0.18 x the opening's width (ASSUMED typical stacking allowance for pleated drapery, not a cited standard): as far beyond the opening as the wall pier allows, the rest overlapping the glazing edge, as a short-pier install does -- for a garden/glazed door this is capped so the two stacks still leave 0.914 m clear to walk through (F.BODY, card mitton-path-of-travel-min); a window carries no such cap. The heavy layer closes across the opening at night; the sheer layer stays open in both states (its job is daytime diffusion, and the closed heavy layer already gives the night blackout/dim-out). ASSUMED: track and stacking dimensions, not a specified product.

Garden (lane GI): the decided layout LDG-final-B built into the production scene at age 3: 101 plants, 36 drawn from graded assets, 65 GENERATED from leaf scans (lane FG: 8 species-fidelity, 57 form-class), 0 labelled STAND-INS (generic masses); house, facade, neighbours and street are the production scene's own.

Photometry: iGuzzini Laser Evo D75 (DL AAK3EW, DLN AAIIA6, ADJ AAHENX; verified LDTs); wall washer positions use AAK3EW as a stated substitute; strips, pendants, sconces and markers are GENERIC (named in each caption).

Selected furniture products use measured native glTF bounds and uniform scale; rejected choices remain PROCEDURAL STAND-INS with recorded reasons. Joinery and sanitaryware remain procedural. Pulls, taps, leg styles, sink and cushion forms are ASSUMED details inside each checked envelope.
Finishes are ASSUMED from the taste profile (no finishes answers yet).
Dressing (plants, books, vases, art, pillows) is not design.
C4(e) floor hosts retain modeled finished elevations; oak/underlay and other floor stacks UNVERIFIED. Support capacities and recessed marker housings require construction coordination.

CLIENT DECISION 2026-10-08: two ASSUMED generic over-mirror linear LED bars; no manufacturer product verified; existing generic isotropic photometry family. Finite diffuser/casing transport has not been independently calibrated.
